content.title: Kentucky vs Iowa State score, highlights: Cyclones win big, advance to Sweet 16
content.text: Updated March 22, 2026, 6:48 p.m. ETFollow all of Sunday's NCAA Tournament second round games with USA TODAY Sports' live updates.Iowa State took a 31-30 lead into halftime against No. 7 seed Kentucky in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. That small lead didn't last long.The No. 2 seed Cyclones defeated Kentucky 82-63 to advance to the Sweet 16 on Sunday, March 22, after outscoring the Wildcats 51-33 in the second half. They forced 20 turnovers, which set a new Kentucky record for the most-ever in an NCAA Tournament game.Playing without All-American Joshua Jefferson, Tamin Lipsey and Milan Momcilovic stepped up for the Cyclones. The All-Big 12 duo scored 26 and 20 points, respectively, to pace Iowa State in the win. Lipsey also had 10 assists and five steals.Iowa State now looks forward to the winner of No. 3 Virginia and No. 6 Tennessee and hopefully gets enough rest for Jefferson to return sooner rather than later.Here are the highlights from Iowa State's second-round win over Kentucky:Shop Iowa State Sweet 16 tickets Kentucky vs Iowa State live scoreTEAMS1H2HFKentucky303363Iowa State315182 Kentucky vs Iowa State live updates Iowa State takes down Kentucky with easeIowa State is heading to the Sweet 16 after taking down Kentucky 82-63 despite missing All-American Joshua Jefferson. Tamin Lipsey scores a career-high 26 points in the win, and Milan Momcilovic adds 20.The Cyclones outscore Kentucky 51-33 in the second half to face the winner over No. 3 seed Virginia and No. 6 Tennessee. Kentucky breaks program record for turnovers in NCAA Tournament gameKentucky makes history, although not the good kind. Its 20 turnovers are a program record for the most it has ever surrendered in an NCAA Tournament game.Iowa State has scored 25 points off the Wildcats' turnovers. Iowa State builds lead to 63-45Iowa State has taken complete control in the second half, now leading Kentucky 63-45 after a Tamin Lipsey's step-back midrange jumper. The Cyclones were shooting 26% after the first half, but are up to 43% for the game as the shots are starting to fall.Iowa State has outscored Kentucky 32-15 in the second half and has forced 19 turnovers. Iowa State takes 13-point lead on Nate Heise's layupNate Heise takes it coast-to-coast and drives through the lane and scores as he's fouled. He messes the following free-throw shot but Iowa State still takes a 52-40 lead.Heise, filling in for Joshua Jefferson in the starting lineup, has eight points so far. Iowa State takes 48-40 leadTamin Lipsey and Milan Momcilovic are carrying the Joshua Jefferson-less Cyclones, with 17 and 14 points, respectively, so far. Iowa State leads Kentucky 48-40 with 12:48 to go, thanks to pesty defense that has forced nine steals and 15 turnovers already. Iowa State finding a way despite poor shootingIowa State is shooting 32% from the field with a poor 5-of-20 mark from 3-point range so far, but it still manages to lead Kentucky 41-36 at the under-16 timeout in the second half.Tamin Lipsey is causing trouble for the Wildcats so far, with 15 points with three rebounds and three assists, along with four steals. The Cyclones outscore the Wildcats 22-10 after falling down 20-9 early on. Iowa State shot just 29% from the field, but forced Kentucky to turn the ball over 12 times.Milan Momcilovic leads the Cyclones with 10 points, while Tamin Lipsey has nine points. Denzel Aberdeen leads the Wildcats with 10 points. Kentucky and Iowa State gone coldKentucky holds a 28-23 advantage over Iowa State with 2:52 left in the first half at the final media timeout. The Wildcats have just eight points in the last nine minutes of game time, but still led the Cyclones.Iowa State is just 7-of-28 from the field, including 1-of-14 from 3-point range. Kentucky has taken more 3-pointers (15) than 2-pointers (8). Iowa State uses 9-0 run to get back into gameJust like that, Iowa State is back in the game following a 9-0 run. Kentucky's lead is 20-18 with 9:33 left in the first half. The Wildcats have not scored in 2:11 of game time and have three turnovers in that span. Denzel Aberdeen gives Kentucky double-digit leadDenzel Aberdeen has eight points, and Kentucky is out to an 11-point lead at 20-9 over Iowa State with 11:30 left in the first half. The Cyclones continue to struggle on the field, shooting 4-of-14 so far.However, Iowa State will get three free throws when the game returns from the timeout. Kentucky jumps ahead earlyAided by a 10-0 run, Kentucky leads a Joshua Jefferson-less Iowa State 10-4 with 15:26 left in the first half at the first media timeout.Collin Chandler is already up to six points, splashing in a couple of 3-pointers. The Cyclones are just 2-for-8 from the field to start the game. Kentucky-Iowa State underwayWe're 40 game minutes away from determining the next contestant in the Sweet 16, as the second-round matchup between Kentucky and Iowa State is underway. How to watch, streaming infoThe game is airing on CBS, streaming via Fubo, which offers a free trial to potential subscribers.Watch Iowa State vs. Kentucky in men's NCAA Tournament live with Fubo (free trial)Joshua Jefferson injury update: Will Iowa State star play today vs Kentucky?Iowa State standout Joshua Jefferson will miss Sunday's second-round March Madness game against Kentucky, according to an NCAA player availability report released two hours before tip-off.Jefferson, a second-team All-American, suffered an ankle injury 2 1/2 minutes into the Friday's game and did not return. Cyclones coach T.J. Otzelberger didn't seem too optimistic after the first round game."Right now, we're continuing to evaluate," Otzelberger said. "It appears unlikely, but you never want to rule anything out, so we'll just continue to do what we can in his best interest and we'll be prepared to go either way."Asked what it would take for him to play Sunday, Jefferson said: "I need to feel like myself. …. What you guys have seen all season from me, being able to be versatile on the floor and make the moves I've been making all year."Iowa State vs Kentucky prediction, oddsOdds provided by BetMGM, as of 9:30 a.m., Sunday.∎ Eugene Rapay, Des Moines Register: Iowa State 79, Kentucky 73Potentially being without Jefferson is tough, but if Heise and Killyan Toure can keep scoring as they did in the first round, that'll go a long way for the Cyclones. Iowa State has to stay true to its identity, with physicality and disruptive defense. Kentucky's size and athleticism may present problems, but the Cyclones have depth they can rely on. The margin for error shrinks without Jefferson, but the Cyclones will aim to survive and advance, and hope that he'll be in good shape for next week. ∎ Ryan Black, Courier-Journal: Iowa State 71, Kentucky 68 With a healthy Joshua Jefferson, the Cyclones likely would be close to a double-digit favorite. But if he's hobbled, that hurts Iowa State. And if he's not able to play at all, that's even tougher. Yet it's not as if the Wildcats don't have injury issues of their own. Starting point guard Jaland Lowe has been out since January. And forward Jayden Quaintance would need a miracle to be cleared Sunday.Kentucky used up more energy — physically (going to OT) and emotionally (barely keeping its season alive) — than Iowa State.It'll be a bare-knuckled fight Sunday. But Iowa State will eke out a narrow victory to bring down the curtains on Kentucky's second season under Mark Pope.John Leuzzi: Iowa StateJordan Mendoza: Iowa StateEhsan Kassim: KentuckyBlake Schuster: Iowa StateMoneyline: Iowa State (-220); Kentucky (+180)Spread: Iowa State (-5.5)Over/under total: 146.5
